intent: The i3 shutdown block shows which earners can still push shutdown later, like the gaming-budget block does: '⏻ 22:00 +🧩1h +📖1h +🗂30m +⚙30m →max 23:00'.
scope: Non-goal: no hint in the override or SHUTDOWN states; no change to how shutdown is computed (screen-locker owns that)
changes: earner_hint reads the enforcer's /api/budget .rules.earners and lists those with earned_seconds == 0, using bonus_seconds as the shutdown amount (equal for every earned_time earner today)
'→max 23:00' is appended when the listed bonuses exceed the headroom to SHUTDOWN_CEILING_MINUTES (default 1380, earned_time's ceiling); no hint at all at the ceiling
A dead or erroring server shows the bare time, which still comes from /etc/shutdown-schedule.conf
Efficiency test stubs curl as a dead server and allows 2 execs (bash + curl); new behaviour test runs in the shell-tests CI job

verification.evidence: '⏻ 22:00 +🧩1h +📖1h +🗂30m +⚙30m →max 23:00'; after the LeetCode solve was applied: '⏻ 23:00'
All shutdown hint tests passed (listing, ceiling note, all-earned, 1h30 padding, unknown earner label, server down / ok:false / non-JSON)
All i3blocks efficiency regression tests passed; All gaming_budget checks passed

risks: If an earner's shutdown_minutes ever differs from its gaming_minutes, the hint shows the gaming amount; /api/budget does not expose shutdown amounts.
The 23:00 ceiling is duplicated from earned_time as a default; a registry change needs SHUTDOWN_CEILING_MINUTES or this default updated.
rollback: git revert this commit; the block shows the bare '⏻ HH:MM' again
